title: Hyperpolarization skews butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hyperpolarization skews butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the model the authors propose, hyperpolarized cells present a positively charged outer surface that reduces bacterial viability, so butyrate-producing bacteria are distributed away from hyperpolarized cells and toward the depolarized oncogene-expressing cells, where the resulting butyrate inhibits HDAC and promotes histone hyperacetylation and cell cycle arrest.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Transducing hyperpolarization into cell responses: HDAC1 inhibition

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As a result, distribution of butyrate producing-bacteria is skewed away from hyperpolarized cells in favor of oncogene-expressing cells, which are known to be depolarized pre-neoplastic transformation [43].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “DISCUSSION › Transducing hyperpolarization into cell responses: HDAC1 inhibition”. Scope: Proposed model for Xenopus laevis embryos bearing oncogene-induced tumor-like structures and hyperpolarized remote tissue

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-11: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism makes specific spatial predictions but the necessary bacterial, butyrate, and acetylation maps were not collected. Existing tumor-incidence data cannot distinguish this model from alternative microbiome or HDAC pathways.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Image or sequence butyrate-producing bacteria spatially relative to hyperpolarized and oncogene-expressing cells, measure local butyrate and histone acetylation, and manipulate surface charge independently of Vmem. The full predicted spatial chain must co-vary.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The paper explicitly lacked in vivo butyrate localization and bacterial culture tools.

Antibiotic effects do not establish spatial redistribution.

Surface charge and Vmem effects are confounded.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.75
data existence: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed skew of butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells is a spatial prediction with chemical and histological readouts. Those maps were not deposited with the incidence results, and general butyrate–HDAC datasets from other species lack the embryo geometry. The distribution model needs new or newly released measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map butyrate-producing bacteria, surface charge or membrane voltage, local butyrate, histone acetylation, and cell-cycle state across hyperpolarized host tissue and depolarized oncogene cells. Skew of viable bacteria and butyrate toward the depolarized cells, with HDAC inhibition there, would support the spatial model.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Bacterial attachment and bacterial viability can respond differently to surface charge, so both need to be measured.

No public spatial microbiome or butyrate map exists for these tadpoles.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.18
operationalizability: 0.66
data existence: 0.22
